scope.subject: Anatomy

marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q009.takeaway: Parietal peritoneum is mesothelium: a simple squamous epithelial lining of a serous body cavity.
marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q009.displayText: The parietal peritoneum is lined by simple squamous epithelium, specifically mesothelium. The same epithelial type lines the pleura and pericardium; simple squamous epithelium also occurs in alveoli, endothelium and the thin segment of the loop of Henle.

rationales.b: Stratified squamous epithelium is multilayered and is not the serosal lining of the peritoneum.
rationales.c: Cuboidal epithelium is typical of sites such as thyroid follicles and many renal tubules, not parietal peritoneum.
rationales.d: Columnar epithelium is not the epithelial type forming the mesothelial lining of the peritoneal cavity.

marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q010.takeaway: Thyroid follicles are lined by simple cuboidal epithelium.
marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q010.displayText: Thyroid follicles are lined by cuboidal epithelium: a single layer of cells whose height is approximately equal to their width, usually with rounded nuclei. Other source-listed examples include the ovarian surface, choroid plexus, inner surface of the lens, retinal pigment layer and proximal renal tubules.

rationales.a: Stratified cuboidal epithelium has multiple cell layers; thyroid follicles normally have a single cuboidal layer.
rationales.c: Stratified columnar epithelium is multilayered and does not form the usual thyroid follicular lining.
rationales.d: Columnar epithelium is not the standard epithelial type identified for the thyroid follicular lining in this source.
